title: SLO charter: tiered SLOs, regional circuit breakers, and probabilistic load-shedding for model-serving
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose:
This ticket defines the SLOs, SLIs, and operational policy for region-aware error budgets, circuit breakers, and load-shedding for Redwood model endpoints. The goal is to provide a single, auditable charter that platform teams can use to configure per-endpoint SLOs, implement automated regional failover decisions, and enable safe, graceful load-shedding under capacity pressure.

Scope:
- Per-endpoint and per-model variant SLO definitions (latency and success rate) for three service tiers: developer (best-effort), standard (default), and enterprise (SLA-backed).
- SLI measurement primitives and how they are computed in the telemetry pipeline (request-level labels, model_variant, route, region, and token counts).
- Error budget accounting: rolling windows, burn-rate logic, and cross-region reconciliation for distributed budgets.
- Circuit breaker rules and thresholds based on sliding-window metrics (error-rate, p95/p99 latency, and queue depth).
- Probabilistic load-shedding strategies (token-aware and request-priority-aware) with safe guards and staged ramping.
- Runbook and rollout plan for updating production endpoints and the Console, plus observability dashboards and alerts.

Background and motivation:
We currently have heterogeneous SLO implementations and ad-hoc failover behavior per service. As usage grows across regions and model families (some models are naturally slower or noisier due to longer context or model size), we need a unified, principled approach that: 1) treats model characteristics as first-class in SLOs, 2) reconciles error budgets across regions without causing thrashing, and 3) provides predictable failure modes (circuit-breakers + load-shedding) to protect tail latency and downstream customers.

Proposed SLIs (measurement details):
- Latency-success SLI: fraction of requests that complete without error and with response-generation latency 〈= SLO threshold per tier (ms). Compute at request level, tag by model_variant, route, region, and priority header. Aggregates: rolling 30d, 7d, 1h windows.
- Latency quantiles: p50/p95/p99 measured on generation-only time (server-side token loop), excluding client network time.
- Availability SLI: request success rate (2xx + well-formed partial streams) per endpoint. Define failure codes that count as errors (5xx, timeouts, malformed outputs).
- Efficiency SLI (experimental): tokens-per-second throughput under steady-state load for model variants (used to inform load-shedding heuristics).

Tiered SLO targets (example, configurable per endpoint):
- Developer: availability 99.0% (30d), p95 latency <= 1200ms (short context models)
- Standard: availability 99.9% (30d), p95 latency <= 500ms
- Enterprise: availability 99.95% (30d), p99 latency <= 800ms, plus per-route latency SLOs defined as needed
Note: model variants may carry adjusted latency SLOs (e.g., 7B vs 70B). We will publish a model-profile catalog of recommended SLO baselines.

Error budget accounting and cross-region policy:
- Each endpoint has a primary error budget computed on a 30d rolling window. Burn-rate calculation uses a 1h and 6h short-term burn estimator to detect fast burns.
- Regions maintain a local view of the budget with periodic reconciliation (every 5 minutes) against the global budget using vector clocks to avoid races.
- If a region exhausts >80% of its local budget in a short window (6h) while global budget remains healthy, the region escalates to local mitigation (probabilistic shedding and circuit-breaker warm-up) rather than immediate failover. This reduces cross-region thrash.
- Global exhaustion triggers pre-defined rollback and traffic-route policies (see Rollout & Failover below).

Circuit breaker and failover rules:
- Trip conditions (sliding window): error-rate > 3% OR p99 latency > 2x SLO threshold OR queue depth sustaining > 250ms head-of-line delay for 3 consecutive windows (1m windows x 3).
- Half-open probing: after tripping, allow a controlled probe rate (1-5% of baseline traffic) to the affected region/model to assess recovery. Probes pass only if latency and error rates meet per-tier thresholds.
- Regional failover policy: primary->secondary failover activated when region-level circuit breaker trips AND global error budget burn-rate exceeds 1.5x expected. Failover must be gradual (traffic ramp 0 -> 100% over 5 minutes) with continuous monitoring and automatic rollback on signs of systemic issues.

Probabilistic load-shedding strategies:
- Token-aware shedding: drop or short-circuit requests probabilistically based on expected downstream token cost and current budget burn rate. High-token requests assigned a higher drop probability.
- Priority-aware shedding: respect request-priority headers; enterprise routes are exempt until their dedicated budget is exhausted. Developer tier first, then standard.
- Graceful degradation: when shedding, return structured fallback responses (e.g., cached summary, retry-after header, or degrade to a smaller model variant) rather than opaque errors. All fallback types must be annotated in telemetry.

Observability and dashboards:
- Required metrics: per-endpoint request_count, error_count, gen_latency_ms (histogram), queue_depth_ms, token_count, model_variant, region, priority.
- Dashboards: SLO health (30d/7d/1h), error budget burn chart, circuit breaker states, region reconciliation status, shedding rates by tier.
- Alerts: SLO burn-rate thresholds (short-term and long-term), circuit breaker trips, failed probes, and automated-failover events. Alerts tied to runbook steps and on-call rotations.

Runbook and operational playbook (high-level):
1) Detect burn-rate spike -> on-call triage -> evaluate whether model variant or region causes spike.
2) If regional circuit breaker trips: enable local shedding and increase probe sampling as outlined.
3) If global budget at risk: initiate controlled failover using Canary flows and monitoring.
4) Reconcile post-incident: cause analysis, update model profiles, and adjust SLO baselines if needed.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (canary): implement SLI computation and dashboards for a small set of endpoints (5 routes, mixed tiers) and verify metrics. (2 weeks)
- Phase 1 (policy engine + prob. shedding): enable circuit-breakers and token-aware shedding in canary region; validate probe logic. (3 weeks)
- Phase 2 (regional reconciliation + failover): enable cross-region budgeting and gradual failover on a subset of endpoints. (2 weeks)
- Phase 3 (wider rollout): roll policy to all production endpoints, publish model SLO catalog, and update Console with per-endpoint SLO controls. (3 weeks)

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Burn reconciliation frequency vs. control-plane load: 5m vs 1m reconciliation chosen as compromise; can be tuned.
- How to set initial per-model SLO baselines for newly onboarded models: propose an automated bootstrap using offline benchmarks + initial 7d warm-up window.
- Whether to expose per-route SLOs to customers in Console or keep them internal for platform enforcement. Proposal: expose SLOs for enterprise customers only by default.

Acceptance criteria (must be met before Done):
- SLI computation is implemented and validated for 5 pilot endpoints (logs and dashboards exist).
- Policy engine can trip and half-open probes correctly for region-level circuit breakers in canary.
- Token-aware and priority-aware shedding implemented and exercised under load tests; metrics show expected reductions in tail latency.
- Error budget reconciliation proves stable under simulated cross-region divergence (test harness in GH).
- Runbook and Console UI mockups reviewed by SRE, Runtime, and PM teams.

Deliverables:
- SLO charter doc (this ticket + Confluence page)
- Telemetry PR to add SLI dimensions (GH: runtime telemetry PR)
- Policy-engine PR (GH: runtime/circuit-breakers) + e2e tests
- Dashboards and alert rules (Grafana/Datadog links)
- Runbook and incident playbook

Circuit breaker trip and half-open probe behavior tested in canary region with automated assertions
Token-aware and priority-aware load-shedding logic reduces tail latency under stress tests without crossing enterprise budgets
Cross-region error budget reconciliation shows stable convergence in 95% of simulated divergence scenarios
Runbook, dashboards, and Console mockups reviewed and signed off by SRE/PM/Runtime teams
decisions: 2026-02-25: Use 30d rolling window as canonical error budget period and expose 1h/6h burn-rate windows for short-term detection
2026-03-01: Reconciliation interval set to 5 minutes to balance timeliness and control-plane load
2026-03-04: Adopt probabilistic token-aware shedding rather than strict request-count throttles to better respect customer priorities
2026-03-08: Enterprise tier will be exempt from probabilistic shedding until dedicated budget is exhausted
